methodology: Privately reviewed the saved user-message render callback gate and page-level edit submission routine. Published data contains source ordinals and authored operation summaries, not captured source.

stages.behavior: The typed user-message renderer supplies an edit callback only when its user item matches an eligible identity, edit actions are available, and targeted reply or certain attachment conditions do not suppress editing.
The conversation page accepts an edit request containing the targeted message identity, replacement prompt, render format and inline hints, and delegates to its local submission routine.
The submission routine refuses a competing edit, an unsupported conversation origin, or an ineligible active conversation state before changing request state.
It resolves the editable message context, including selected model and original parent message; a missing target produces a defined client failure.

The routine trims replacement text, builds a message representation with editing format and hints, obtains attachments, and rejects a completely empty replacement unless permitted by structured non-text content.
Where an incompatible active response exists, it requests stop and awaits closure before submitting the edit; certain conversation origins or session states bypass this stop step.
After any asynchronous stop, it checks that the request identity and target-message data still match and that conversation streaming state is suitable.

It delegates to the shared completion-submission helper with the edited message, selected model, attachments, replacement prompt and the original editable message's parent identity. The client call is visible, not the resulting server graph.
A finally block clears the edit-busy flag; the page callback converts exceptions into a user-facing edit-failure notification with error classification.

interpretations: The submitted edit includes an original parent-message identity, consistent with creating a replacement continuation rather than deleting a message node in place; this is a client request property, not verified server branching.
An editing form's availability depends on user-message and conversation state guards, so not every displayed user message necessarily exposes the control.
Completion submission after an edit is a separate operation from whether an edited response successfully streams or becomes selected.
unverified: The exact DOM form lifecycle of every editing variant and its keyboard shortcuts.
Whether a particular edited message produced a new branch, overwrote existing server state, or became the selected client node.
Network delivery, server acknowledgment, stream completion and outcomes of the edit-failure notification.
The entire submitted payload and API contract beyond the reviewed client-side argument roles.
privacy: No original request endpoint, original file name, source function symbol, copied prompt, source code, personal data or account identifier is published.
module_ordinal_contract: 1-based property order of the original saved bundle's module registry. Values refer only to this capture and do not disclose original minified module names.
